accuracy.evidence: Zone limits match NOAA Ocean Exploration and Smithsonian Ocean: sunlight (epipelagic) 0–200 m, twilight (mesopelagic) 200–1000 m, midnight (bathypelagic) below 1000 m with no sunlight. The light meter uses exp(−d/43 m), which leaves about 1% of surface light at 200 m (the NOAA/clear-ocean figure for the base of the euphotic zone) and the lab forces it to zero from 1000 m. Plants (seaweed, phytoplankton) need light for photosynthesis, so they are shown growing only in the sunlight zone. Animals checked: sea turtles breathe air and feed near the surface (green turtles on sea grass, leatherbacks on jellyfish); lanternfish are mesopelagic and migrate up at night to feed (diel vertical migration); deep-sea anglerfish live mostly 1000–4000 m and use a bioluminescent lure. Marine snow (sinking dead material and droppings) as the main deep food source is from NOAA Ocean Service. All parameterised answers checked at their corners (p2 1000−200..900, p4 200−10..190, m6 200−20..180, m9 300..900−200).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented child ideas about the deep sea: light is the same all the way down (step 1 prediction, challenge tag 'same', p1), zone order reversed or twilight on top (step 2 prediction and placing feedback, tag 'order', p3), the midnight zone is dark only at night (tag 'night', m1, m2), plants grow in every zone (step 3 prediction 'In all three zones' then the twilight and midnight plants fail, tag 'plant', p5), and nothing can live or eat where nothing grows (step 5 prediction 'Nothing at all', tag 'snow', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdepth is about light versus depth: a submarine whose depth drives a light meter and a three-band depth scale, zone names placed by depth, plants that grow or fail by zone, animals placed by zone and marine snow tweened from the sunlight zone to an anglerfish drawn with a glowing lure. flagocean (shore/shallow/deep and salt water), flagseaneed (food, shelter, oxygen) and flagovar (size and shape variety) do none of this, and the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees the result before the text names it: the light bar empties and the readout says 'none' only when they reach 1000 m; zone names are accepted only in depth order with a reason when wrong; the plant count only rises for sunlight-zone plants while deeper ones stay grey with a cross; the anglerfish's food counter rises only when sinking food reaches it. Each step closes with the one-line rule the child has just shown.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'It stays bright all the way down' or 'gets brighter near the sea floor' (the meter falls to zero), the deepest zone (twilight is the tempting pick; the placement feedback corrects it), 'In all three zones' for plants (twilight and midnight plants do not grow), and 'Nothing at all' for deep animals' food (marine snow feeds the anglerfish).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six feedback messages keyed to the slip: 'same' (water soaks up light), 'order' (most light to least), 'plant' (plants need light to make food), 'night' (midnight is the name; it is dark all the time), 'lure' (a glowing lure only helps in the dark) and 'snow' (food sinks from above). In-lab feedback also names the slip for each wrong zone name and each wrong animal home (turtle must breathe air, lanternfish hides in dim light, anglerfish hunts in the dark).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the readability limits (learner kid ≤ 6.5, adult ≤ 9.5). Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (soaks up, dim, like snow); the Greek-root zone names are kept for the adult text only. Canvas labels are 13–18 px with white pills on the water so they read on every band; pad buttons are short (Dive deeper, Plant at the top, → bottom).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12%). Each kid paragraph carries one idea (light fades, three zones with depths, plants need light so life is near the top, deep food and bioluminescence); adult paragraphs give the scientific zone names, why light fades with the 1% figure, four named mistakes with marine snow, and what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark themes for every step after Show me: the three bands, 0/200/1000 m pills and zone names fit without clipping; the submarine readout stays on screen at 1000 m; plants were moved right after the first shot put a twilight plant over its zone label; the anglerfish emoji (a fishing rod) was replaced with a drawn anglerfish with a pale outline so it shows on the black midnight band. Pad buttons use the young-learner size (56 px minimum).

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Dive deeper/Go up, pick a zone name then → top/middle/bottom, Plant at the top/middle/bottom, pick an animal then a zone, Drop food. The canvas aria-label and the visible description update with each state change through tell(). The walk gate's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA, both themes, desktop and iPhone 13) reported no violations and no console errors.
